summary.text: A previously healthy 24-year-old man was referred from primary care with a platelet count of 25 x10^9/L and a 1-week history of frontal headache, severe dizziness and generalized weakness, with recent fever and no bleeding or bruising. Dengue fever was the provisional diagnosis and he was admitted.

Intravenous fluids and empirical antibiotics were started and platelet units were prepared for a possible transfusion. Follow-up platelets were 40 x10^9/L, inflammatory markers were within normal limits and malaria testing was negative.

The peripheral smear showed excessive platelet clumping with morphologically normal platelets. EDTA and citrate samples gave platelet counts of 42 and 191 x10^9/L in the text (Table 3 prints 157.0 for citrate), confirming EDTA-dependent pseudothrombocytopenia.
He remained stable and asymptomatic, was discharged in good condition after 2 days of observation and was counseled; dengue serology after discharge was negative.
